chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abū al-Ḥasan, from his father, from Ibn Abī Umayr, and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Ḥasan ibn al-Walīd, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, and Ibn Abī Umayr, from Muʿāwiya ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said: When you have finished your circumambulation (ṭawāf), go to the Standing Place of Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him) and pray two cycles (rakʿatayn), and make it in front of you, and recite in the first of them the Surah of al-Tawḥīd: 'Qul huwa Allāhu ʾAḥad', and in the second: 'Qul yā ayyuhā al-kāfirūn'. Then testify (tashahhud) and praise Allah, and extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and ask Him that He should accept from you.

And these two cycles are the obligatory ones. It is not disliked for you to pray them at any time you wish, at the rising of the sun and at its setting. And do not delay them for a while after you have circumambulated and finished, so pray them.

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He is Allah, the One

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and method for the two-cycle prayer after Tawaf?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith establishes ṣalāt al-ṭawāf as a confirmed Sunnah (often termed 'fariḍah' in the context of ritual completeness) rather than a strict obligatory duty, emphasizing its immediate performance at Maqām Ibrāhīm to maintain the spiritual continuity of the pilgrimage rites. The specific recitation of Sūrat al-Tawḥīd and al-Kāfirūn highlights the theological pillars of monotheism and distinctiveness in worship, while the instruction to pray immediately after ṭawāf underscores the importance of not delaying ritual acts of devotion. This ruling reflects the Ja'fari school's view on the flexibility of timing for this prayer, distinguishing it from the fixed times of the five daily prayers.
